output:
**Subject: Re: Our plan for next year**

Appa, Amma, Kiran, Divya and everyone,

First, I’m so happy you’re coming, Amma and Appa. The thought of having you here for the summer makes me ridiculously happy, and Anika has already made a laminated welcome timetable. Tuesdays are apparently reserved for “Paati teaches us rasam”. Appa, the vegetable patch is waiting for your drumsticks.

Kiran, you’re right. I should have told you earlier and brought you into the conversation before the visa paperwork began. That’s on me, and I’m sorry. I started it because the agent needed my sponsor letter and bank statements, but that was exactly when I should have looped you in. You shouldn’t have had to hear about it once things were already under way.

For a bit of background, the idea actually came from Appa when we spoke in August. Rohan showed him the vegetable patch on video and he said, “I could grow drumsticks there.” We started talking from there, but I should have shared that conversation with you rather than letting it come as a surprise.

Your questions about Appa’s heart are important. I’ve spoken to Dr. Prakash, and he’s agreed to review Appa in March before they fly, then do a video consultation in July. He’s also happy to share his notes with me. I’ve obtained a travel insurance quote with pre-existing cardiac cover, at about £640 each for the six months. The agent says it covers the stent, but I’ll make sure we check the policy wording and any conditions carefully before we buy it. You’re right that we can’t assume visitors will get free NHS treatment.

If Appa needs urgent care, Leicester Royal is about 15 minutes from our house. I know half the cardiology team, though of course I hope we won’t need to call on them. The annexe at the back is finished too: it’s all on the ground floor, with no steps and its own shower with a grab rail. I’ll send you the insurance details and what I have from Dr. Prakash so you can have a proper look.

And yes, six months is a long time, especially for Amma when she hasn’t been away from home for more than six weeks since Paati died. The plan is the first week of April until the end of September 2027, within the six-month limit for each visit on the UK long-term visitor visa. But it doesn’t have to be an endurance test. Amma, if you want to go home sooner, you can; the return ticket will be flexible. We can see how you both feel as we go.

I’m sorry too that we didn’t talk about Ganesh Chaturthi before this. One possibility is that Amma and Appa fly from Leicester to Pune in September and finish their trip there. Or, if it works for you, the Pune lot could come here in August. I’d love that, and I’ll cover your flights. Neither has to be decided now—I’d like to hear what you all think.

Could we have a family video call this Sunday at 4 pm UK time, 9.30 pm India time? It would be good to talk everything through together, including anything we haven’t thought of yet.

Lots of love,  
Meera
